findings.title: vat_for() rounds half-to-even, so 0.5-cent VAT rounds down on even cents
findings.body_markdown: `vat_for()` quantizes with `Decimal.quantize()` and no rounding argument (line 14), which is `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. German invoicing requires half-up, and `vat_for(1250, "DE")` would produce 237 instead of 238.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × reachable internally × blast radius 0.50 × file tested, symbol not × churn 0.20
notes: clamped to info: repro passed at head

"""Repro for a Witness finding in app/billing/tax.py::vat_for.

Claim: vat_for() rounds half-to-even.
"""

from app.billing.tax import vat_for


def test_half_cent_vat_rounds_up():
    assert vat_for(1250, "DE") == 238

findings.title: invoice_tax_total() sums rounded line taxes, so the total drifts from the rate
findings.body_markdown: Rounding each line before summing (line 41) makes the invoice total differ from `rate * net` by up to one cent per line. Three lines of 333 cents at 19% give 189 where the invoice rate gives 190.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × proven × reachable internally × churn 0.20 × blast radius 0.10
